first_impression.reaction: Sophie here. James proposed with a placeholder ring and we're choosing the real one together, so I Googled this. The intro is calm, there's no 'dream ring' gush, and the four lenses, especially travel, are more than the usual Pinterest gallery. I skimmed the takeaways and the table, then read halo, hidden halo, three-stone and the destination section properly. I skipped the vintage definitions and the Mohs numbers.

journey.quote: Each style gets a plain description, a "suits you if" line and a "think twice if" line, so you can shortlist two or three types of engagement rings before you sit down with a jeweller.
journey.reaction: Good. That's exactly what I want: a shortlist before we walk into a jeweller and get talked into something.

journey.quote: this is the style that rewards the side-profile ceremony shot. Brief your photographer so the angle isn't missed.
journey.reaction: That's the kind of small, insider detail I'd never have thought of. It's the first line that's about our wedding, not just the ring.

journey.quote: Channel- and bar-set bands can be difficult to resize, especially when stones extend far around the band, and full eternity bands are generally treated as not resizable.
journey.reaction: Honest trade-off. My fingers swell in summer, so that's useful.

journey.quote: GIA calls the bezel a practical choice for exactly that life.
journey.reaction: By the tenth 'GIA says' it starts to feel like a summary of GIA's site. It's credible, but I'm reading it for your take, and I can't hear yours much.

journey.section: Check your insurance covers overseas travel
journey.quote: Tell your insurer your travel dates and check the policy covers loss and damage as well as theft.
journey.reaction: Practical. That goes on the list for the wedding trip too.

journey.section: From the ring to the wedding abroad
journey.quote: A Wedded Advisor plans venue, travel, vendors and payments anywhere in the world, as one point of contact from first idea to the last dance.
journey.reaction: One contact is what we want. But every planner says this. Nothing here shows what it means for 80 guests, half flying in, or my grandparents getting from the airport. 'Last dance' is a touch brochure-y.

journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor will take it from there, in your time zone and quoting in AUD.
journey.reaction: Quoting in AUD actually matters to me. Currency surprises are a real worry, so that's a small win.

unanswered_questions: What does 'plans venue, travel, vendors and payments' cover for guests: flights, airport transfers, older relatives?
Is there a real wedding, with venue and date, I can look at?
Does quoting in AUD mean the price is locked in AUD, or just converted at the time?
would_share_with: James: the quick comparison table, so we can each pick two
Not my parents; this is ring stuff, not wedding stuff

cta_reaction.quote: talk to Wedded Concierge about a wedding abroad
cta_reaction.why: Low-pressure, which I like, but I came here for rings. I'd browse destinations first and only enquire after reading a couple of planning posts and seeing a real wedding.

top_3_changes: Give the brand's own view in a few places instead of leaning on 'GIA says' in almost every section, so it reads as advice from people who've done destination weddings.
Back up 'one point of contact from first idea to the last dance' with one concrete example, ideally a real wedding with venue and date, or one line on guest travel.
Expand the ring-on-the-wedding-trip angle (photographer brief, who holds the rings on the day), since that's where the page feels uniquely useful to us.

checks.check: Every journey point and the CTA reaction has an exact quote from the draft
Stayed in character as Sophie & James (Sydney, early research, 14 months out, wary of 'end-to-end' claims)
No invented brand facts; gaps listed in unanswered_questions
HTML comments and fact markers ignored as invisible
No invented problems; no hard turn-offs found

assumptions: Assumed the couple is engaged with a placeholder ring and choosing the final style, since the persona is 14 months out from the wedding.
